title: Christmas in Fukuoka 2026: Hakata, Tenjin and Kihinkan markets
description: Compare Fukuoka’s 2026 Christmas market dates, hours and closures at Hakata, Tenjin and Kihinkan, with a route that separates markets from lights.
intro: Christmas in Fukuoka does not have one opening date. For a first Christmas Advent route, choose three venues: Hakata Station square, the west-side City Hall plaza in Tenjin and the space outside Kihinkan. Their markets start on different days, and Tenjin has two exceptional November closures.

This guide compares the venues and explains how to combine them without mistaking illumination for an operating market. Organiser and prefectural tourism information was read on 7 November 2026. The archive photographs show earlier-season lights at Hakata and the buildings at the other venues; they do not document the 2026 Christmas installations.

quickFacts.label: Kihinkan
quickFacts.value: 11 November–25 December; market and lights have different hours

sections.heading: 1. Hakata: a market outside the station
paragraphs: The Hakata market occupies JR Hakata Station Square, immediately outside the Hakata exit. The organiser identifies access through the JR station and the Airport and Nanakuma subway lines. It is a useful stop to connect with arrival or departure, provided the market hours actually fit your transport schedule.

The published period is 7 November to 25 December 2026. Ordinary hours are 16:00–23:00 on weekdays and 12:00–23:00 on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays, with last orders at 22:45. On 7 November it starts at 16:00, while 24 and 25 December have a published noon opening.

The programme includes stalls, food and music, but a photograph of lights does not establish a performance at the moment you arrive. Market entry is advertised as free, with purchases and refreshments separate. If carrying luggage, work out storage and your return to the platform before entering busy circulation areas rather than obstructing the station approaches.

sections.heading: 2. Tenjin: find the west side and check the closed dates
paragraphs: TENJIN CHRISTMAS ADVENT takes place at Fureai Square on the west side of Fukuoka City Hall. The building is a useful landmark, but the market is not outside any façade: our photograph shows the east-northeast front in 2025. Use the plaza name and organiser’s map to identify the actual event approach.

The venue announces 14 November to 26 December 2026, closing on 28 and 29 November. The first weekend, 14–15 November, is co-hosted with another event. Ordinary hours are 17:00–23:00 on weekdays and 12:00–23:00 on weekends and public holidays, with last orders at 22:45. On 21 November it closes at 21:30.

Published access points include Tenjin on the Airport Line, Tenjin-Minami on Nanakuma and Nishitetsu Fukuoka (Tenjin). These are distinct references: choose the one matching your journey rather than assuming every exit reaches the same spot. A noon opening is announced for 24 and 25 December. Check any changes before organising an entire evening around this venue.

sections.heading: 3. Kihinkan: FESTA de SANTA has an earlier market finish
paragraphs: FESTA de SANTA occupies the area in front of the historic Kihinkan building in Nishinakasu. The organiser lists Nishinakasu 6-29 and approaches from Nakasu-Kawabata and Tenjin-Minami, each with an indicative five-minute walk. The outdoor event space should not be confused with admission inside the historic building.

The announced period is 11 November to 25 December 2026. Normal market hours are 17:00–22:00 on weekdays and 12:00–22:00 on weekends and public holidays, with last orders at 21:45. Illumination is listed until midnight, which does not automatically extend food service or stall operation.

The documentary photograph shows the building in August 2017 without Christmas installations. It helps identify the location, while the current programme supports the seasonal information. If arriving after Tenjin, allow for Kihinkan’s earlier market finish. Consult the day’s programme for a particular meal or performance rather than inferring it from the lighting hours.

sections.heading: Which dates let you combine all three venues?
paragraphs: For a trip based on these three markets, their published calendars overlap from 14 November to 25 December, excluding Tenjin’s closures on 28 and 29 November. This is the intersection of market dates, not confirmation of every performance, product or additional installation.

Before 11 November, only Hakata in this selection has opened according to its dates. Kihinkan joins it on 11–13 November, while Tenjin begins on the 14th. On 26 December Tenjin remains within its published period, but Hakata and Kihinkan have ended. Do not extend the market season automatically because another Fukuoka illumination continues into January.

sections.heading: Divide the route without spending the evening transferring
paragraphs: One approach gives Hakata its own outing and combines Tenjin with Kihinkan on another. This leaves time to browse and eat without treating the next venue as a countdown. With one evening, begin with whichever opens first on your date and protect Kihinkan because its market closes at 22:00.

Check subway routing and the journey back to your accommodation using the stations identified by each venue. This guide does not publish a frequency, fare or last-train time without an operator-specific check. Tenjin and Kihinkan’s relative proximity may favour walking, but the actual choice should account for crossings, mobility, rain and the exact event entrance.

sections.heading: Entry, refreshments, mugs and market rules
paragraphs: The organiser’s FAQs advertise free market entry and free performances while asking visitors not to occupy seats simply to reserve them. Food, drinks and shopping are not included. Check prices and allergens at the stall before ordering, especially where someone has dietary requirements.

Venue-specific mugs are part of the offer, but the organiser says they are not sold on their own. Avoid planning a mug-only purchase from a photograph. Published rules also prohibit bringing food and drinks into or out of the venue; check current instructions before arriving with a meal bought elsewhere.

Choose spending priorities before starting the circuit. Buying a drink or souvenir at every venue is optional, and a free-entry itinerary need not become a sequence of repeated purchases. Taking time to compare the actual offer is more useful than assuming each market has the same stock or menu.

itinerary: Two-outing option: use Hakata on the afternoon or evening that fits your station arrival. Reserve a separate outing for Tenjin and Kihinkan, avoiding 28–29 November if Tenjin is essential.

One-evening option: first identify whether it is a weekday, weekend or exceptional date. Choose the order around openings and your return. Reach Kihinkan with a margin before its 21:45 last orders; lights until midnight do not replace the market.

Before going: read the day’s notices, check any performance that matters to you and confirm refreshment conditions. A satisfying route may include only two venues if that gives you time to eat and stroll without rushing.

faq.question: When do Fukuoka’s 2026 Christmas markets begin?
faq.answer: In this selection Hakata begins on 7 November, Kihinkan on 11 November and Tenjin on 14 November. Calendars differ, and Tenjin closes on 28–29 November.

faq.question: Is there an entrance charge for these markets?
faq.answer: The organiser advertises free entry. Food, drinks and purchases are separate; check any conditions attached to a particular activity or product.

faq.question: Can I keep shopping at Kihinkan until midnight?
faq.answer: That does not follow from the lighting hours. The market publishes a 22:00 close and 21:45 last orders, while illumination is announced until midnight.

faq.question: Can I buy just the souvenir mug?
faq.answer: The organiser’s FAQs say mugs are not sold alone. Check the current offer and associated purchase before planning that transaction.

conclusion: Plan Fukuoka by venue and date rather than one citywide Christmas calendar. Hakata, Tenjin and Kihinkan provide different settings; separating markets, music, lights and the journey home makes a better route than trying to complete everything without a pause.
